According to the Financial Times, the latest court documents show that OpenAI is disappointed with the adoption of ChatGPT through Apple Intelligence, and pointed out that this integration feature has 'performed far below expectations' since its launch in 2024. The following are the details.

OpenAI is asking the court to rule before the trial begins

In August 2025, Elon Musk said that X, which has been merged into SpaceXAI, will sue Apple and OpenAI for allegedly colluding to suppress competitors in the AI field. The dispute stems from an agreement between OpenAI and Apple to integrate ChatGPT into Apple Intelligence and Siri.

The subsequent litigation has actually gone beyond the App Store ranking issues that Musk publicly complained about. X and SpaceXAI also accused Apple of trying to curb the development of 'super apps', including X's plan to transform itself into an 'everything app'.

In the weeks and months that followed, the companies involved先后 submitted arguments, complaints and defences to the court. Apple and OpenAI also argued in multiple filings that their agreement is not as exclusive as the lawsuit claims. The court documents also revealed new details about the workings behind this collaboration.

Some of these details were exposed in documents filed by OpenAI today. According to the Financial Times' initial report, OpenAI 'expressed disappointment that Apple users showed such low interest after the two companies reached an agreement in 2024 to power "Apple Intelligence" with ChatGPT'.

The report content is as follows:

Wednesday's court documents pointed out that when the agreement was reached in 2024, OpenAI had hoped to leverage Apple's promotional and brand power to create a 'halo effect', attracting more Apple Intelligence users to subscribe. However, one month after the ChatGPT integration feature was launched, this feature had 'a noticeably slow start', and OpenAI began to lower its weekly active user projections. The documents also mentioned that by the summer of 2025, it had become clear that 'Apple's integration of ChatGPT has performed significantly below expectations'.

The report pointed out that the documents filed today contain several redacted conversations, but the unredacted parts show that OpenAI executives were worried that Apple might 'want to find another AI partner as soon as possible'.

When Apple Intelligence was first announced in 2024, Apple's Senior Vice President of Software Engineering Craig Federighi said in an interview that Apple ultimately hopes users can choose between different AI models, and explicitly mentioned that Google Gemini would be a potential future integration option.

Although that specific collaboration ultimately failed to materialise, Apple has since switched to using Google's Gemini model to power parts of the new Siri AI, and Xcode has also been expanded to support coding agent tools provided by Anthropic, Google, and OpenAI.

The most-liked comment was posted by OliveCocktail

As others have said, when I want to use ChatGPT, I just open its dedicated app directly. I actually have the same preference, because I don't want to mix all my voice requests together. I'd rather let Apple handle my personalised, context-related stuff. I've never figured out the privacy implications of using the ChatGPT 'integration', and I don't want to spend time figuring it out, because I know I won't use it. In contrast, I'm completely at ease with the privacy protections of Apple Intelligence or Siri.

Speaking of today's documents, the Financial Times pointed out that the documents also暗示 that the way Apple implemented ChatGPT may be one of the reasons for the low adoption rate, because this integration feature is turned off by default.

Finally, according to Reuters, OpenAI is also citing SpaceX's recent securities disclosure documents to undermine SpaceXAI's claim that Apple's cooperation has harmed competition. OpenAI pointed out in its documents that SpaceX's IPO registration statement is full of disclosures that are 'completely contrary to the competitive harm alleged in the lawsuit'.

Based on these reasons, OpenAI is asking Judge Mark Pittman to rule in its favour on SpaceXAI's antitrust allegations before the trial begins. The case is currently scheduled for trial next January.
